neighbours.label: the word before 'reputation' or 'rap' in 'have/get/earn a (bad) reputation' frames
fire: For decades, sharks have been given a bad name by films.
Carbohydrates have gotten a bad reputation in recent diet books.
Pit bulls often suffer from a bad reputation they do not deserve.
The small town quickly earned a reputation for its friendly bakers.
Online dating used to have a bad image among older people.
Fast food chains have long had a poor reputation for nutrition.
Over the years, the critic acquired a reputation as a harsh judge.
Unfortunately, the old hotel developed a bad reputation for noise.
quiet: For decades, sharks have been given a bad scare by divers.
Carbohydrates have gotten a bad mention in one chapter of the book.
Pit bulls often suffer from a bad hip as they get older.
The small town quickly earned a grant for its new library.
Online dating used to have a bad interface on older phones.
Fast food chains have long had a poor selection of salads.
Over the years, the critic acquired a house near the coast.
Unfortunately, the old hotel developed a bad leak in the roof.

notes: Top examples: 'got a bad rap', 'given ionization a bad reputation', 'earned a reputation'. Fires before the reputation noun, so near misses use 'bad' or 'a' in other frames.
